<p style="font-size:14px;">
The American Robin (*Turdus migratorius*) is a widespread and adaptable migratory songbird that occupies a variety of habitats, including forests, shrublands, grasslands, agricultural areas, and urban environments. In the boreal region, the species is commonly associated with forest edges, open woodlands, and areas with diverse vegetation structure that provide suitable nesting sites and foraging opportunities. Its ability to use disturbed and human-modified landscapes contributes to its broad distribution and resilience to many local habitat changes. However, shifts in landscape composition, changes in vegetation structure, and alterations to habitat availability may influence local habitat suitability. This vulnerability assessment evaluates potential exposure to landscape changes and assesses factors that may influence habitat conditions for American Robin within the assessment area.
</p>
